ai_show_review.summary: First Lovelight debut and fiery Alligator jam in a high‑octane early show
ai_show_review.blurb: The set features the inaugural Turn On Your Lovelight and a scorching Alligator that capture the band's emerging psychedelic drive. Jerry's guitar tears through the Lovelight while Bob lays down a thick rhythm on Alligator. The soundboard recording is clear enough for a 1967 tape, making it essential listening for early‑Dead fans.
ai_show_review.review: The August 5, 1967 show at Toronto’s O'Keefe Center delivers an electrifying glimpse of the Grateful Dead in their formative blaze. Right out of the gate the band launches into the first ever recorded Turn On Your Lovelight – Pigpen’s gritty vocals roar and Jerry Garcia’s lead guitar rips through the mix, setting a combustible tone that carries straight into a tight, driving Alligator where Bob Weir’s full‑bodied rhythm chops anchor the jam. Phil Lesh holds down a solid bass foundation while Billy Kreutzmann keeps a steady pulse, allowing the group to ride the high energy of their early psychedelic cohesion. Though captured on vintage 1967 tape, the soundboard source is remarkably clear and well‑balanced, giving listeners an intimate window onto a pivotal moment in Dead history.

best_recording.reason: Clear soundboard capture of the historic first Lovelight and a high‑energy Alligator, offering the most complete and listenable version of this early show

key_highlights: First known performance of Turn On Your Lovelight
Explosive Alligator jam with searing guitar work
High‑energy early Dead set showcasing Pigpen's vocal fire
Soundboard recording provides unusually clear audio for a 1967 tape

band_performance.Jerry: Tearing up the place with powerful, soaring lead guitar on Turn On Your Lovelight and driving chops throughout Alligator.
band_performance.Bob: Rich, full rhythm‑guitar tone on Alligator that locks in tightly with the band’s groove.
band_performance.Pigpen: Gritty, commanding vocals on Turn On Your Lovelight add intensity and drive to the performance.
